prompt: Consider only the four one-line integer inputs -3, -1, 0, and 2. The program is run fresh for each input. Which of those inputs raises IndexError, and why? Assume the input line is supplied, so parsing and end-of-input errors are not at issue.

options.text: -3 and -1. Both are negative, and Python lists reject every negative index.
options.feedback: A negative index can be valid: -1 selects the last item, 8. For this two-element list, -3 is too far back and raises IndexError. Only -3 crashes among the listed inputs.

options.text: -3 and 2. Both are out of bounds for this list, and and evaluates items[index] for both inputs.
options.feedback: You correctly identify the crash for -3, whose upper-bound check is true. But and short-circuits: for 2, the check 2 < 2 is false, so items[2] is never evaluated. Only -3 crashes.
options.partial_reason: Correct: identifies -3 as an invalid index that is actually evaluated and crashes. Incorrect: also predicts a crash for 2 by evaluating the right-hand side of and despite a false left-hand side.

options.text: Only -3. It passes index < len(items) but is below the valid negative-index range. Input 2 fails the first check, so and skips indexing.
options.feedback: Yes. The valid indices are -2, -1, 0, and 1. Input -3 reaches an invalid lookup; -1 and 0 access positive values; 2 short-circuits to the else branch.

options.text: None. The check index < len(items) rejects every invalid list index before the lookup can run.
options.feedback: That check only enforces an upper bound. It accepts -3 because -3 < 2, but -3 is invalid for a two-element list. A safe check allowing Python's negative indices would also require index >= -len(items).

options.text: -3 and 0. The index -3 is too far back, and list positions start at 1, so items[0] also raises IndexError.
options.feedback: The failure for -3 is real, but Python lists use zero-based indexing. items[0] is the first value, 4, so input 0 prints positive rather than crashing. Only -3 crashes among these inputs.

explanation: For a two-element built-in list, negative indices -2 and -1 are valid; -3 is not. The upper-bound check accepts -3 and the lookup raises IndexError. Input -1 accesses 8 and input 0 accesses 4, so both print positive. Input 2 makes index < len(items) false; and skips the lookup and the program prints outside. Only -3 crashes among the four listed inputs.

expected.stderr_contains: IndexError: list index out of range

verification.rationale: Run the exact displayed snippet once for each of the four inputs in the prompt. Assert exact stdout and exit code, and a stable IndexError substring for the one deliberate exception. Manual reasoning checks valid negative indices and short-circuit control flow.
verification.limitations: The finite input set is exhaustive only for this prompt, not for all possible stdin. Execution alone does not validate half credit, misconception diagnosis, or distractor appeal.
